stores.name: users

fields.name: created_at
fields.note: Timestamp on the row that represents the person.

erasure.note: The repository defines only create_document and get_profile as routes; no route, command or job deletes a user row.

stores.note: SQLAlchemy table holding the user record.

stores.name: documents

fields.name: title
fields.note: Free-form string supplied by the user of the document.

fields.name: body
fields.note: Unconstrained text column on a row linked to a user.

erasure.note: User.documents carries cascade="all, delete", but no code path deletes a User, so the cascade is never triggered.

stores.note: SQLAlchemy table for documents, joined to users by user_id.

stores.name: uploads

fields.name: Key
fields.note: The object key is built as docs/<user_id>/<document_id>.pdf in document_key.

fields.name: Body
fields.note: The uploaded document bytes passed through from the route.

erasure.note: storage.py defines only put_object; there is no delete_object call and no deletion path in the repository.

stores.note: Amazon S3 bucket written by upload_document.

fields.name: owner_email
fields.note: The user's email is copied into the indexed document.

erasure.note: search.py calls es.index only; no delete call exists and no deletion path in the repository reaches this index.

stores.name: events

fields.name: email
fields.note: The user's email is the payload body published to the queue.

erasure.note: publish_document_created writes the payload; nothing in the repository consumes or removes it.

stores.note: RabbitMQ queue published to by publish_document_created.

stores.name: nightly_dump

fields.name: email
fields.note: Listed in DUMP_COLUMNS and read off each row by getattr.

erasure.note: write_dump overwrites a single JSON file at DUMP_PATH; the repository carries no cron entry, TTL or lifecycle rule stating how long the dump is kept.

stores.note: JSON file written by the write_dump job from the users and documents tables.
